2016_094_051716mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of May 17, 2016 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, combining recognitions, the April 12 and April 19 minutes, the March 2016 Treasurer's Report and six action items. The Treasurer's Report records total disbursements in the period of $11,666,802.42, of which $9,480,837.72 was check disbursements. On consent, the Board adopted a resolution supporting the Oakland Intermediate School District 2016-2017 budget under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, stating that its support was “for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624.”

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 PM, May 17, 2016, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
Baker Middle School "Shark Tank" winners, 8th graders guided by Anne Costello, Lisa Gaglio and Colin Quinn. Outstanding Support Staff Award: eighteen (18) individuals nominated, with Craig Matthes (Classroom Aide/Manager, Terrace Cafe, Athens High School) named Employee of the Year and forwarded for the county-wide Betty Campion Award. Retirees of the 2015-2016 school year received clocks from Vice-President Karl Schmidt as Jordan Harris read each name, among them Anne Lenihan (Costello, 46 years), Steven Gottlieb (Athens, 40) and Mary Fairweather (Bemis, 38). A resolution marked National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 2-6, 2016, and Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence president Al Robinson recognized recipients of the 79 grants the foundation funded this year.

**Minutes on consent**
April 12, 2016 workshop (President Philippart, 6:05 p.m. to 8:27 p.m., Mr. Miletti absent) covering the March cash position and budget report, land valuation follow-up, professional development and a facilities review follow-up. April 19, 2016 meeting (Vice-President Schmidt presiding, 7:02 p.m. to 8:37 p.m., approximately 200 in the audience), at which 42 outstanding-teacher nominees were honored and Adam Burns, Jason Cichowicz and Laura Kemp advanced to Oakland Schools; resolutions 16-035 and 16-036 accepted Great Northern Consulting Group proposals for Section 23 not to exceed $20,000.00 and Sections 11 and 16 not to exceed $34,500.00, plus due diligence not to exceed $51,200, all from the Capital Maintenance Fund, each 6-0 with Philippart absent.

**Action items**
Consent item 5.D adopted a resolution supporting the Oakland ISD 2016-2017 budget under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, to be forwarded no later than June 1, 2016. Personnel ratified three-year contracts running July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2019 with TESPA (tentative agreement April 26, 2016) and TESA (April 27, 2016; ratified May 11, 2016). Business authorized a Master Equipment Lease with Great America Financial Services for a copier fleet, no greater than four years at not to exceed $73,374.72 per year, plus an Applied Imaging cost-per-copy maintenance agreement at not to exceed $.0032 per impression for Canon monochrome and $.0049 black and .059 color for Canon color equipment, as General Fund expenditures. Under Public Act 419 of 2004 the Board supported Barbara DeMarco and Connie R. Williams for two six-year Oakland Schools Board seats ending June 30, 2022, to be voted June 6, 2016. A bond update was received as a report requiring no action.

**April 12, 2016 workshop minutes.** At the Administration Building, President Philippart called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Schmidt and Underwood present and Mr. Miletti absent; Superintendent Machesky and administrators Dziatczak, Griffor, Harris and West attended with approximately three other members of the audience. Business covered the March cash position and budget report and a land valuation follow-up; teaching and learning covered professional development; the superintendent gave a facilities review follow-up. Adjourned 8:27 p.m.; submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**April 19, 2016 meeting minutes.** At the Services Building, Vice-President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Underwood present, Dr. Philippart not in attendance, and approximately 200 members of the audience. Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning Mark Dziatczak was liaison to the community-volunteer Facilities Study Team, with Gary Wood, retired principal of Costello Elementary, as Community Facilitator; certificates also went to Nicole Balintfy, Michael Chrobak, Scott Courtney, Erik Edoff, Walt Feifer, Suzanne Hamilton, Dale Inman, Michael LaPree, Daniel Murphy, Kristi Roncelli, Anne Sackrison, Sunilkumar Sivaraman, Pete Van der Harst and Pete Ziegenfelder. Natalie Haezebrouck of Leonard Elementary was co-recipient of the Michigan Reading Association Teacher K-6 Educator Award for her Guided Reading Academy. A record 42 individuals were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award, three advancing to Oakland Schools: Adam Burns (Athens TV Production, AP English and Innovations) as high-school Teacher of the Year, Jason Cichowicz (Schroeder, 5th grade) as Elementary Teacher of the Year, and Laura Kemp (Baker, 7th grade science) as Middle School and Overall Teacher of the Year. Resolution 16-034 approved the consent agenda, including the February 2016 Treasurer's Report and the March 1, March 15 and March 17, 2016 minutes, 6-0 with Philippart absent. Resolution 16-035, moved by Fleming and supported by Edmunds, accepted the Great Northern Consulting Group proposal for Section 23 not to exceed $20,000.00. Resolution 16-036, moved by Edmunds and supported by Miletti, accepted the Great Northern proposal for Sections 11 and 16 not to exceed $34,500.00 and authorized due diligence not to exceed $51,200 covering a Department of Environmental Quality wetland determination and site walk, a formal topographic survey with wetlands, and concept plans for a request for proposal; both were Capital Maintenance Fund expenditures passing 6-0 with Philippart absent. Student representatives Matt Moroski, Victoria Malkoun, Snigdha Suvarna and Maxwell Fanroy reported. Adjourned 8:37 p.m.

**Item 5.D, Oakland ISD budget.** Under Section 624 of the Revised School Code, as amended, the intermediate school board must submit its proposed budget no later than May 1 each year, and each constituent board must, not later than June 1, adopt a resolution expressing support or disapproval and submit objections and proposed changes. The Troy Board resolved that it had reviewed the proposed Oakland ISD budget and expressed its support, adding that "it is the responsibility of the Intermediate School District to be responsible for its own operations, including adoption of its budget" and that its support "is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624 of the Revised School Code." The secretary or designee was directed to forward the resolution to the intermediate school board or its superintendent no later than June 1, 2016, and conflicting resolutions were rescinded; certification cites a regular meeting held May 17, 2016 noticed under the Open Meetings Act, 1976 PA 267, as amended. No ISD dollar amounts appear.

**Items 6.A and 6.B, personnel.** A tentative agreement with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA), comprised of paraprofessionals and skilled-trades employees, was reached April 26, 2016 and ratified by the membership (the ratification day is left as a placeholder). A tentative agreement with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association/MEA/NEA (TESA) was reached April 27, 2016 and ratified May 11, 2016. Both contracts run three (3) years, July 1, 2016 through June 30, 2019, with red-lined versions in the Board packet; no wage percentages or dollar figures are stated.

**Item 8, copier lease.** After a Technology and Business Services review of existing copiers and installations, the Board was asked to authorize the Superintendent or designee to execute a Master Equipment Lease Agreement with Great America Financial Services for a fleet of copiers for a period no greater than four (4) years at an annual cost not to exceed $73,374.72 per year, and a Cost per Copy Maintenance Agreement with Applied Imaging not to exceed $.0032 per impression for Canon Monochrome Equipment and $.0049 black and .059 color per impression for Canon Color Equipment, also not to exceed four (4) years, both as General Fund expenditures.

**Item 10.A, Oakland Schools Board election.** Under Public Act 419 of 2004 the Board must designate a representative to the 2016 electoral body and identify supported candidates by resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days before the election and considered at not less than one public meeting. The resolution names Barbara DeMarco and Connie R. Williams for two (2) positions on the Oakland Schools ISD Board of Education, each for a six (6) year term ending June 30, 2022, with the designated representative directed to vote for them at least on the first ballot at the June 6 election. A supporting email from Kathy Boike, Executive Assistant in the Oakland Schools Office of the Superintendent and Board of Education, sent Monday, May 09, 2016 4:25:09 PM to the OCSA ListServ, notes that both filers are unopposed incumbents so no "Meet the Candidates" forum will be scheduled; that ballots must be cast in person from 5:30 to 7:30 PM Monday, June 6, 2016 in Conference Room B at Oakland Schools, 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, MI 48328, absentee ballots being prohibited; that resolutions may be adopted no earlier than May 16, 2016 and must be faxed to 248.209.2206 by end of business Friday, June 3, 2016; and that questions go to Sherry McMillan at 248.209.2062. Attachments included mcl-380-614 Revised School Code.pdf, 2016 Sample Local Board Resolution.pdf and OS BOE 2016 Election Timeline Revised.2.pdf.

**Item 10.B, bond update.** A brief update on the status of bond projects throughout the district was to be provided; the item is a report with no action necessary.
